title: Naghtognk (Corlears Hook)
summary: A Manhattan placename for Corlears Hook, linked with Dutch forms Nechtauk and Nechtank and interpreted as a landmark-tree name.
map_geometry_source: approximate Corlears Hook / Lower East Side marker; not an exact landmark tree location
introduction_content: Naghtognk names Corlears Hook on Manhattan Island. The form is connected to Schoolcraft and to Dutch spellings recorded as Nechtauk or Nechtank.
history_content: Corlears Hook location, the Dutch forms, and the one-tree interpretation are brought together here. The later Rechtank entry should be reviewed as a cross-reference rather than a separate site unless evidence shows otherwise.
translation_content:
Alternate forms include Nechtauk, Nechtank, and the later cross-reference Rechtank. The interpretation used here is one tree, compared with related Algonquian forms for a single tree; another source-derived explanation involving sand remains tentative.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are fundamental for reconstructing the diachronic development of communities without written records, encoding unique historical and cultural data.”

— Hanjun Hua and Francesco Perono Cacciafoco, Kula Toponyms: Preserving the Cultural–Linguistic Landscape of Eastern Alor (2026), abstract
whereintheworld_content: The point is an approximate general marker at Corlears Hook on the Lower East Side of Manhattan. It represents the historic locality, not an exact landmark tree location.
